answer: Each identity posts a binding day-ahead position — how much energy it will buy or sell tomorrow at which hours — and settlement compares the position against its actual metered flow. A spiral of fake positions collapses at settlement because deviations are charged at imbalance prices, so only a party with a real flexible load or generator can afford to play. The terrace of positions is public, the cedar of the commitment is the signed schedule, and a Sybil gains nothing from ten positions it cannot physically deliver.
